stem.text: In a thermodynamic process, an ideal gas absorbs \(1.5\ \mathrm{kJ}\) of heat and expands from its initial volume of \(20\ \mathrm{L}\) to \(35\ \mathrm{L}\) under constant pressure of \(30\ \mathrm{kPa}\). Calculate the change in internal energy of the gas.

answer_scheme.heading: Answer scheme with step-by-step student hints

steps.title: Calculate the work done by the expanding gas
steps.student_hint: Convert pressure and volume to SI units. The gas expands, so ΔV > 0 and the work done by the gas is positive.

steps.title: Apply the first law of thermodynamics
steps.student_hint: Heat absorbed by the gas is positive (Q = +1.5 kJ = +1500 J). Because the gas does work on its surroundings, subtract W from Q.

steps.title: Substitute values to find the internal energy change
steps.student_hint: Use the work found in Step 1. A positive result means that the internal energy of the gas increases.
